title: Value equality and hash codes
idea: `equals` decides when two objects mean the same value; `hashCode` must agree with it, so equal objects land in the same hash bucket.
points: Equal objects must return equal `hashCode` values; unequal ones may collide.
Hash collections pick a bucket by `hashCode`, then confirm the match with `equals`.
Build both from the same immutable fields, or let a `record` generate them.
Value objects compare by content; entities compare by a stable id.

messages.label: contains(b)
messages.note: The set holds `a`, which equals `b` by content.

messages.label: hashCode()
messages.note: The hash picks one bucket. Only that bucket is searched.

messages.label: hash value
messages.note: `hashCode` is overridden from the same fields, so `b` hashes like `a` and lands in `a`'s bucket.

messages.label: equals(a)
messages.note: Only an entry with the same hash in that bucket is compared with `equals`.

messages.label: true
messages.note: Fields match, so `equals` confirms the value.

messages.label: true
messages.note: Both methods agree, so the lookup succeeds. Break either and it fails.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: `equals` overridden, `hashCode` not. Equal keys get lost in hash collections.

walk.text: `equals` compares code and size, so two SKUs with the same fields are equal.
`hashCode` is still the identity-based one from `Object`. The contract is broken.
Direct comparison works, which is why the bug survives simple tests.
The set searches the copy's bucket, misses `a`, and then stores a duplicate.
The map lookup with an equal key finds nothing and returns `null`.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: A final value class with matching `equals` and `hashCode`, and the record version.

walk.text: Validate and normalise in the constructor, so equal meanings get equal fields.
Same-reference shortcut, a type check that also rejects `null`, then field comparison.
`Objects.hash` over exactly the fields used in `equals` keeps the contract.
The class is final with final fields, so equality cannot drift after insertion.
A record generates both methods from its components; only validation is hand-written.
`merge` finds the existing entry with a fresh equal key, so one entry holds both amounts.

pitfalls: Overriding `equals` without `hashCode`: `HashSet.contains` returns false for an equal copy.
Mutating a field used by `hashCode` after insertion: the entry becomes unreachable.
Letting subclasses add fields to `equals` breaks symmetry; make value classes final.

quiz.why: `ArrayList.hashCode` depends on its contents. After the edit the set looks in the wrong bucket, though the entry still counts toward `size`.

takeaway: Same fields in `equals` and `hashCode`, and never mutate a key.
